title: The denial saga — one $315 office visit, denied and rebuilt
dxAfter: Concussion without loss of consciousness (initial encounter) + external-cause code + nausea — a more specific, complete diagnosis set

steps.label: Claim submitted
steps.detail: The visit is billed to Blue Cross as claim L1007201490 — a $315 charge for a moderate-complexity office visit (CPT 99214).

steps.label: Denied
steps.detail: Blue Cross denies the claim with reason code 16 — 'claim lacks information needed to adjudicate.' Nothing is paid; the denial image posts twice.

carc.plain: Claim lacks information needed to adjudicate

steps.label: Charge voided (correction)
steps.detail: A billing specialist voids the original charge as a 'Correction' and reposts a brand-new charge in its place — the new charge points back at the old one, preserving the audit trail.

steps.label: Payment reversed
steps.detail: On the same claim ID, the remittance posts a 'reversal of previous payment' of −$315, unwinding the denied claim so it can be re-adjudicated cleanly.

steps.label: Rebilled — corrected claim
steps.detail: The new charge is resubmitted as L1007233830 (accepted) then L1007233831 (closed), tagged with the free-text note 'CORRECTED CLAIM.' The diagnosis is upgraded from a single unspecified code to a specific concussion diagnosis with an external-cause code — fixing exactly the 'missing information' the denial flagged.

steps.label: Paid
steps.detail: The corrected claim adjudicates normally: of the $315, Blue Cross allows $198.91, writes off $116.09 (above the allowed amount), assigns $19.89 to the patient's coinsurance, and pays the provider $179.02.

carc.plain: Above the plan's allowed amount (sticker-price markdown)
